correctness.rationale: A rule forbids precisely one row pattern on r=k+1 independent columns. The first moment is the number of labelled rules times q_k^n. If two supports share s<r columns, the two bad patterns either conflict or together specify 2r-s bits, so joint rule satisfaction is at most (1-2a+a²2^s)^n, with a=2^(-r). Distinct heads on one support have disjoint bad patterns and joint probability (1-2a)^n. The log of the proper-overlap bound is strictly convex, with endpoint values 2 log q_k and log q_k, proving the stated strict chord inequality. The disjoint-column dependency graph is valid for the whole neighborhood. Pair counts of order m^(2r-s) and m^r then give vanishing Stein–Chen sums at m on the critical scale and, by the same estimates, vanishing relative variance above it. Below it Markov applies. The limit t^r/k! counts unordered premise positions and the labelled head. For lower arities including zero, -log(1-2^(-u))/u is strictly decreasing in u, so the expected counts vanish in the k-window. The first moment for empty premise support has the same exponential base as the (k-1)-premise implication count and also vanishes there. Hence the claimed simultaneous minimality and support property holds only in the stated critical regime. Inspected the supplied checker as bounded corroboration, not as a proof of the limit.

evidence: Bognár's strict-regularity criterion compares sums S2 of squared numbers of allowed completions over shared coordinates against s^(2-l/r), with s the total number of allowed atoms and l the overlap. It is general over fixed-arity Boolean relations.

For one forbidden atom, put D=2^(r-l) and s=2^r-1. Every l-coordinate marginal has 2^l-1 completion counts D and one D-1, so S2=(2^l-1)D²+(D-1)². Dividing by 2^(2r-l) turns the strict-regularity condition into precisely the frozen strict joint-avoidance chord inequality; it holds by the interpolation checked for correctness. Distinct atom sets on the same support have strictly fewer than s common allowed atoms.

Bognár's Theorems 1–2 treat threshold and critical existence; equations (42)–(45) bound the total overlap contribution. Stark states the unary Poisson law and illustrates the method for other Boolean relations. The specific covering-array paper was not available in the attempted retrieval and is not used as positive or negative coverage evidence.

evidence: Bognár uses the graph of distinct relation events with an edge for shared selected indices. At order two his one-overlap contribution is precisely the sum of joint event probabilities over overlapping distinct pairs (up to using unordered instead of ordered pairs); (42)–(45) bound it and make it vanish at the critical scale for strictly regular relations. The same-support term uses strictly fewer common atoms for distinct events. For this relation the usable support choices are r times binom(m,r), yielding mean t^r/k! from the one-event probability (s/2^r)^n.

That overlap sum is the only nontrivial local-dependence Stein–Chen term. The product-of-means term is O(m^(2r-1) q_k^(2n))=O(1/m) at criticality, and all events outside a support neighborhood jointly depend on disjoint input columns. Therefore the stated TV Poisson count follows from prior overlap estimates and the standard inequality, irrespective of the garbled extraction of the right-hand side of (33).

A smaller-premise rule is another one-forbidden-atom relation with fewer columns; an unsupported k-premise forbids the single pattern 1^k. Their expected counts decay at the r=k+1 scale by comparing the elementary first-moment exponents, including the empty premise. Absence with high probability gives inclusion-minimal premises immediately.

The count upgrade and simultaneous first-moment corollaries here apply existing estimates without new overlap control. No inference of a full count law from mere equality of void probabilities is made.

originality.rationale: Bognár (1962) directly treats the same independent uniform random subsets, general fixed-arity Boolean relations, and their critical-window and overlap estimates. The k=2 implication is the complement dual of a printed strictly regular example; every higher fixed k is the same one-forbidden-atom specialization of the criterion. The earlier paper is not credited with an explicit TV count theorem. Instead, its already established negligible overlapping-pair sum, together with first moments and independent disjoint column sets, yields that theorem by the standard local-dependence inequality without a further probabilistic estimate. The hierarchy and support statements add first-moment comparisons of the same one-atom relations, not a distinct surviving result.
residual_risks: Bognár's theorem statement is an existence result; whether those exact passages state the finite TV law is not asserted. The decision uses the verified overlap argument and its direct consequence.
The formal-context algorithms and covering-array texts were not recoverable in the attempted routes; they are not the basis of a negative literature claim.
